item.title: Can the chemical potential and the many-body correlated phases of a two-dimensional dipolar fluid be approximated analytically? A Quantum Monte-Carlo study of a universal behavior of dipolar excitons
item.description: arXiv:2611.33289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in quantum many-body physics is to connect microscopic interactions to experimentally accessible macroscopic states of matter, where correlations extend across multiple length scales. Using quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of two-dimensional repulsive dipolar bosons, recently realized across various experimental platforms, we show that correlations within the dipolar fluid lead to an unexpected simplification. Specifically, we find that these correlations induce a pronounced depletion region around each particle that suppresses short-range physics and yields an emergent universality, where the fluid is governed by dipolar interactions rather than material-specific details. Exploiting this universality, we establish a unified, quantitatively validated analytical framework for the dipolar fluid, taking indirect (interlayer) excitons as a model system. We show that analytical interaction energies derived in an earlier study agree with exact QMC results across three correlation regimes: a classical gas, a quantum gas, and a high-density liquid. In contrast, the widely used uncorrelated plate capacitor formula severely overestimates the numerical values. Building on these expressions, we show that the chemical potential is accurately captured by a three-component decomposition: an ideal Bose-gas kinetic term, a regime-dependent dipolar interaction term, and a high-density quantum confinement term. Finally, we address a key experimental challenge: extracting exciton densities from measured energy shifts. Our QMC-benchmarked calibration curves for typical gallium arsenide (GaAs) and transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures offer a reliable tool for experimentalists to determine both the fluid's density and collective state. This universal framework extends to other two-dimensional systems, including ultracold dipolar atoms and polar molecules.
item.dc:creator: Yotam Mazuz-Harpaz, Michal Zimmerman, Snir Gazit, Ronen Rapaport

item.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2611.33306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Stornati, Piotr Sierant, Emanuele Tirrito

item.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.33274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy $\Delta>1$, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point $\Delta=1$, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For $\Delta>1$, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. At $\Delta=1$, we provide evidence from fluctuating hydrodynamics for the emergence of the KPZ Pr\"ahofer--Spohn scaling function in dynamical correlations and trace it to the finite coupling of the largest particles to a continuum of slower ones, with long-ranged velocity fluctuations. Our framework shows how universal dynamical two-point correlations coexist with distinct model-dependent current statistics.
item.dc:creator: Jitendra Kethepalli, Andrew Urilyon, Jacopo De Nardis

item.title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
item.description: arXiv:2611.33944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the two-dimensional (2D) Gross-Pitaevskii model for a Bose gas, the naive dimensional non-equilibrium wave-turbulence power-law prediction for the direct energy cascade coincides with thermal equilibrium and therefore carries no energy flux. We resolve this degeneracy by deriving a logarithmically corrected spectrum that supports a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales. A systematic asymptotic expansion of the wave-kinetic collision integral determines the logarithmic exponent to be 1/3, while the small-scale dissipation scale sets the upper cutoff in the logarithmic correction. Regularization of a marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale yields an estimate of the spectral prefactor for asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales. Simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic equations support the predicted spectral shape. Over finite spectral ranges, the correction produces apparent power laws steeper than the dimensional prediction, offering a possible explanation for the steep spectra observed in 2D Bose gas experiments. Our approach provides a systematic framework for constructing wave turbulent cascade spectra when the power-law prediction is degenerate with thermodynamic equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Ying Zhu, Jason Laurie, Giorgio Krstulovic, Sergey Nazarenko

item.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
item.description: arXiv:2611.33987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Asari, Masaya Kunimi, Tetsuro Nikuni

item.title: Fate of an impurity strongly interacting with a thermal Bose gas
item.description: arXiv:2508.06493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We spectroscopically study mobile impurities immersed in a homogeneous bosonic bath (a box-trapped Bose gas), varying the bath temperature and the strength of impurity-bath interactions. We compare our results to those for a quasipure Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), and find that for strong impurity-bath interactions, the spectra narrow with increasing temperature, while the impurity energy shift is suppressed. Near the critical temperature for condensation, many-body effects still play an important role, and only for a nondegenerate bath, the system approaches the classical Boltzmann-gas behavior. The key spectral features are reproduced within the theory of an ideal Bose polaron.
item.dc:creator: Ji\v{r}\'i Etrych, Sebastian J. Morris, Simon M. Fischer, Gevorg Martirosyan, Christopher J. Ho, Moritz Drescher, Manfred Salmhofer, Zoran Hadzibabic, Tilman Enss, Christoph Eigen

item.title: Information-Theoretic Diagnostics of Collective Modes and Vortex Dynamics in Rotating Two-Dimensional Bose-Einstein Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2604.24557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a two-dimensional rotating Bose gas confined in a symmetric anharmonic trap, employing the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method for bosons (MCTDHB). We study states ranging from vortex-free configurations to multicharged (giant) vortices, prepared by tuning the rotation frequency, and analyze their response to sudden interaction and trap quenches. In vortex-free states, interaction quenches induce regular breathing-like dynamics, whereas in the presence of giant vortices they lead to symmetry-breaking surface excitations. In contrast, trap deformations that excite quadrupole-like modes produce stable oscillations in vortex-free condensates but trigger rapid, irregular, and effectively chaotic multimode dynamics in multicharged vortices. To characterize these processes beyond conventional density and phase observables, we employ information-theoretic (IT) measures, including marginal and joint spatial entropies, mutual information, and Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, supplemented by an angular-resolved KL measure that quantifies azimuthal density redistribution and symmetry breaking. We find that chaotic splitting is accompanied by a pronounced growth of information-theoretic indicators, signaling the buildup of many-body correlations and increasing complexity in the system dynamics. Our results demonstrate the extreme sensitivity of giant vortices to excitation protocols and establish IT measures as quantitative global diagnostics that complement conventional observables by characterizing spatial redistribution and correlations during complex vortex dynamics.
item.dc:creator: L. A. Machado, N. D. Chavda, B. Chatterjee, M. A. Caracanhas, B. Chakrabarti, A. Gammal, R. P. Sagar

item.title: Tomographic Electron Flow in Confined Geometries: Beyond the Dual-Relaxation-Time Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2503.14461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hydrodynamiclike electron flows are typically modeled using the Stokes-Ohm equation or a kinetic description that is based on a dual-relaxation-time approximation. Such models assume a short intrinsic mean free path $\ell_e$ due to momentum-conserving electronic scattering and a large extrinsic mean free path $\ell_\text{MR}$ due to momentum-relaxing impurity scattering. This assumption, however, is overly simplistic and falls short at low temperatures, where it is known from exact diagonalization studies of the electronic collision integrals that another large electronic mean free path $\ell_o$ emerges that describes long-lived odd electron modes---this is sometimes known as the tomographic effect. Here, using a matched asymptotic expansion of the underlying Fermi-liquid kinetic equation with multiple electron relaxation times, we derive a transport theory for tomographic flows in arbitrary smooth boundary geometries. Our key results are a set of governing equations for the electron density and electron current, their slip boundary conditions (which are applied at diffuse boundaries), and boundary layer corrections near diffuse edges. We find that the tomographic effect strongly modifies previous hydrodynamic theories for electron flows: In particular, (i) a local equilibrium is established in the bulk, where the flow is governed by Stokes-Ohm-like equations with significant finite-wavelength corrections, (ii) the velocity slip condition at the boundary is strongly modified and not accounted for by the widely used hydrodynamic slip-length condition, (iii) a large kinetic boundary layer of width $\sim\sqrt{\ell_e \ell_o}$ arises near diffuse boundaries, which is much larger than in conventional near-hydrodynamic theories, and (iv) all these effects are strongly suppressed by an external magnetic field. We illustrate our findings for electron flow in a channel.
item.dc:creator: Nitay Ben-Shachar, Johannes Hofmann

item.title: Quantum rotation sensing from superintegrability
item.description: arXiv:2605.09709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Detection based on quantum principles such as entanglement has the capacity to achieve finessed levels of sensitivity, bringing transformative impacts to applications. In this study, we propose a rotation sensing protocol using an extended Bose-Hubbard model in a four-site configuration. The design, based on a simple population imbalance measurement to quantify rotation, profits from the property of superintegrability. The implementation of the sensing protocol achieves rotation-detection sensitivity scaling as $N^{-3/2}$, where $N$ is the number of particles. Remarkably, the sensitivity lies close to the quantum Cram\'er - Rao bound. Our results illustrate superintegrability opportunities for advancing the field of quantum sensing.
item.dc:creator: Leandro Hayato Ymai, Karin Wittmann Wilsmann, Joel Bacellar Neves, Arlei Prestes Tonel, Jon Links, Angela Foerster
